rationale: A coherent and correctly-signed consolidation of the archive's two best-performing velocity legs, but it is an incremental blend rather than a new mechanism, and the claim that level and its own first difference are "not mechanically linked" is overstated since ΔATO and ATO are positively correlated in the cross-section.

Replacing a one-year DELTA with a five-year TREND of the same turnover series is essentially a lookback reparameterization of TurnoverImprovementValue, and the underlying asset-turnover-change effect is already a published anomaly (Soliman's DuPont ΔATO), so the incremental information content is low.

A legitimate and well-posed decomposition test of whether the velocity channel runs through throughput or margin, though EBITDA/(act−che) is mechanically margin × turnover rather than a clean isolation of "profit conversion," so the interpretation of a positive result will be ambiguous.

The stated rationale that the two legs avoid a "shared-denominator confound" is wrong — both legs are driven by low operating working capital (act−che appears in the velocity denominator and the reversal numerator), so they are positively correlated by construction, and one parent leg carries a wrong-signed FMB t-stat (−1.68) that the composite is likely to inherit.

The diagnosis is sharp and honest — differencing the two industry ranks strips the common B/M component to test whether the high-alpha/zero-Sharpe liquidity cluster is a tradable composition effect or an FF5 hedging artifact — though the reviewer should note the residual is close to a price-scaled net-operating-assets tilt already partly covered by SoftCapitalBackedPriceTrap.

The expression does not implement the stated payout hypothesis: dvc/assets is typically an order of magnitude smaller and less variable than ΔNWC/assets and is zero for a large share of firms, so the signal is dominated by −ΔNWC scaled by assets, i.e. a near-duplicate of the already-tested working-capital accrual leg interacted with value.
